    bootstrapping.Rmd

    Bootstrapping of Embeded Standard Setting

    Overview

    How to use bootstrapping for ESS

    Fit Embeded Standard Setting 

    library(EmStanS)
    fake_data <- genFakeDataSet(ngca = 3, 
               cor_val = 0.2,
               n = 30,
               nlevel = 3,
               ntable = 5,
               npanelist = 5,
               sdinp = 1,
               ecinp = 0,
               100,300)



fake_data

# Or you can use your own data structured by the following table.
    res <- emstans(data = fake_data,
               grades = c(1, 2),
               location = "Loc_RP50",
               method = "weight",
               smooth = FALSE)

    Bootstrapping

    bootstrapping() resamples one unit’s items with replacement (each keeping its location and modal aligned level) and re-estimates the cut scores in every sample. One unit at a time; seed makes the draws reproducible.

    boot_res <- bootstrapping(res, "M1-All", n = 100, seed = 1)
boot_res
#> Bootstrap of modal cut scores for M1-All (100 samples, item locations, exact minimum)
#>  cut_level   n  mean    sd median   min   max  q2.5 q97.5 estimate
#>     Level2 100 125.7 15.52  131.4 106.8 164.1 106.8 158.0    131.4
#>     Level3 100 256.7 15.27  254.5 220.2 296.1 237.7 295.6    254.5

    By default each sample uses the sampled items’ locations as candidate cuts and takes the exact ESS minimum, the same estimator as emstans(). The earlier EmStanS bootstrap, a jittered grid of candidate cuts with a GAM-smoothed minimum, is available with grid = "jittered":

    bootstrapping(res, "M1-All", n = 30, seed = 1, grid = "jittered")
#> Bootstrap of modal cut scores for M1-All (30 samples, jittered grid, smoothed minimum)
#>  cut_level  n  mean    sd median   min   max  q2.5 q97.5 estimate
#>     Level2 30 127.1 15.98  127.5 100.7 161.2 101.1 161.0    131.4
#>     Level3 30 252.3 15.41  254.9 213.9 283.2 214.7 277.4    254.5

    Report 

    report(boot_res)

    Bootstrap cut scores: M1-All
